OBSERVATION/CONCLUSIONS/RECOMMENDATIONS
AT A GLANCE
 
APPROACH IN THE 10th PLAN AND ANALYSIS OF THE ANNUAL PLAN 2004-05
 
            The Committee is happy to note that the plan allocation of the Ministry of Tourism has been revised to Rs.350 crore in R.E.
 2003-04 and the outlay for the annual plan 2004-05 has also been hiked substantially to Rs.500 crore, which is almost 42% over the
 amount of Rs.325 crore allocated in B.E. 2003-04.  However, the Committee is of the view that plan outlay is not sufficient to explore
 the tourism potential available in the country.  The Committee appreciates the fact that keeping in view the earlier recommendations of
 the Committee, the Ministry of Tourism has been able to fully utilize the funds allocated for the first two years of the 10
th Plan period. 
 The Committee hopes that the Ministry of Tourism will also be able to utilize the enhanced allocation for effective implementation of
 the schemes/programmes for development and promotion of tourism as also for creating high quality and dependable tourism
 infrastructure required to sustain the growth.  The Committee recommends that the plan outlay should be utilised in such a way so that
 it can act as a catalyst to attract the additional investments from other sectors for development of tourism in the country.  In this
 process, the Ministry of Tourism will be in a position to make demand for more allocation of funds at R.E. stage.
(Para 9)
 
EMPLOYMENT POTENTIAL WITHIN THE TOURISM SECTOR
 
The Committee notes with dismay that India's travel & tourism share of total employment is a meagre 2.9 percent which is far
 too less in comparison to other countries of the world.  This is notwithstanding the fact that employment potential of tourism sector is
 higher than Agriculture and Industrial sectors.  The Committee feels that there is an imperative need to integrate tourism with the socio-
economic objectives of the 10
th Plan so that 3.6 million jobs per year can be created through promotion of domestic and international
 tourism and thereby, India's share of international earnings from tourism can be enhanced. The Committee, therefore, recommends the
 Ministry to take proactive measures to exploit the advantages of tourism in generating employment. This is all the more important
 because tourism generates more employment in comparison to other sectors for every rupee invested.
(Para 13)
INTEGRATED DEVELOPMENT OF TOURISM CIRCUITS
 
            The Committee notes that the Ministry of Tourism is laying emphasis on integrated development of six identified tourism
 circuits each year and convergence of all resources and expertise for development of these circuits as destinations of international
 standard.    The Committee is surprised to note that the Ministry has not identified any tourist circuit and sanctioned the development
 works in some of the important States like Sikkim, Orissa, West Bengal, and Jharkhand etc. though these States have full tourism
 potential to attract tourists. However, the Committee feels that the existing limit of Rs.8 crore is insufficient for the development of
 infrastructure for tourist circuit and urges the Ministry to increase the existing limit of Rs.8 crore realistically taking into account the
 actual requirement of funds so that infrastructure facilities required by the tourists within the identified circuits could be provided in an
 integrated and holistic manner.  The Committee also recommends that the Ministry should also identify a tourist circuit in each and
 every States/UTs and develops them by providing all infrastructure facilities required by the tourists with in the circuits so identified. 
 
            The monitoring is crucial to ensure the timely implementation of any project. Therefore, the Committee recommends that the
 monitoring agency should play rather proactive role and do away with the hurdles, if any, to ensure better implementation and effective
 control for completion of development works in each tourist circuit and the Committee should be apprised of the progress in the matter

ASSISTANCE FOR PRODUCT/INFRASTRUCTURE AND DESTINATION DEVELOPMENT
           
The Committee notes that the aim of product/infrastructure and destination development scheme is to improve the existing
 tourist infrastructure and create new tourist infrastructure at important tourist places of national and international importance in the
 country.  The Committee, however, notes with dissatisfaction that several new projects for development of infrastructure at identified
 destinations have been sanctioned by the Ministry of Tourism without fixing any time limit for the completion of these projects.  The
 Committee therefore, recommends the Ministry to develop competitive destinations that match international standards in terms of price,

 travellers.  The Committee also recommends that sufficient allocation to the projects should be made to avoid time and cost overruns as
 a result of which, the investment gets locked in the project.  The Ministry should also fix some physical and financial benchmarks for
 monitoring of the projects.

RURAL TOURISM
 
            The Committee is of the view that Rural Tourism has great potential and prospects in the country as it helps to revive the local
 peoples' interests and pride in their culture, tradition and values besides generating the tourists interest in the customs of the indigenous
 people as it focuses directly on the local people.  The Committee feels that with a growing interest in the intangible culture of different
 countries (i.e. lifestyle, cuisine, ceremonies, music, religion, beliefs, customs and history), there is an enormous potential to encourage
 global tourism in rural areas. The Committee recommends the Ministry to develop some institutional mechanism for supporting,
 promoting and organizing large number of fairs & festivals and handicrafts & craft melas/bazaars in rural areas which will provide
 exposure, recognition as well as additional flow of income to local artisans.  The Committee further recommends that the Ministry
 should actively coordinate efforts for liaising with other Ministries/Departments of Government of India viz. Ministries of Rural
 Development, Environment and Forests, Textiles & Culture etc. and other concerned organisation/agencies for converging of resource
 from that Ministry/Department and increase allocation for tourism sector through the state budgets as tourism has a greater potential for
 creating a large-scale employment opportunity than any other industry in the country.
(Para 29)
 
ASSISTANCE FOR LARGE REVENUE GENERATING PROJECTS
           
The Committee notes with satisfaction that 6 projects have been sanctioned under the scheme of large Revenue generating
 projects and 100% of plan allocation have been released by the Ministry of Tourism during the year 2003-04.  The Committee
 appreciates the efforts made by the Ministry of Tourism in identifying the projects in consultation with the State Governments and
 timely release of funds for sustainable development and management of tourism products. The Committee hopes that the work on these
 projects would be completed within the specified time schedule since the 100 percent finance have been released by the Ministry. The
 Committee is of the view that while identifying the projects under the scheme, the Ministry of Tourism should have more balanced
 regional distribution of projects. The Committee therefore, recommends the Ministry to evolve some mechanism to ensure better
 implementation, effective control and sustained monitoring of projects.
(Para 32)
CAPACITY BUIDLING IN THE UNORGANIZED SECTOR
 
            The Committee notes the capacity building measures taken by the Ministry for providing basic training to the persons engaged in
 unorganized sector of travel & tourism sector and considers that these measures are taken in the right direction.  The Committee further
 notes that orientation training programmes for customs and immigration staff, police officers posted at the airports etc. have also been
 brought under the purview of this scheme. The Committee is of the view that sensitizing Government staff who come in contact with
 tourists can definitely bring about a positive change in their attitude and recommends that these training programmes should be
 arranged more frequently making them more effective and broad based.
(Para 37)
REVIVAL OF TOURISM IN JAMMU AND KASHMIR
 
            The Committee appreciates the Ministry for sanctioning a package for revival of tourism in Jammu and Kashmir which includes
 financial assistance for up-gradation of infrastructure in the valley viz. Shikara owners, Pony wallas, Houseboat owners and Hotel
 owners etc. through the State Government of Jammu and Kashmir.  This is a land crafted by nature's exquisite artistry and the
 Committee feels that promotion of tourism in the state can help achieve enormous benefits for the state as well as for the country.  The
 State of Jammu and Kashmir, on account of its wide and varied products has been a major driver in the growth of Indian Tourism. 
 Therefore, the Committee recommends that to showcase the beauty and splendour of Jammu and Kashmir and also to meet the
 increased demand of tourists, the Ministry should help resolving financial problems of service providers and provide better
 infrastructure for Jammu and Kashmir.  The Committee also recommends that the Ministry of Tourism should have constant contact

DOMESTIC PROMOTIOIN & PUBLICITY INCLUDING HOSPITALITY
 
            The domestic tourism is the foundation of a viable and sustainable tourism industry.  Much of the growth of global tourism has
 been generated by domestic tourism.  However, the Committee is constrained to note that there are no precise estimates of total
 domestic tourist traffic and observes that the potential for domestic tourism is massive and requires focused approach.  The Committee
 recommends the Ministry to put in place accounting system, which can help to assess the importance and significance of domestic
 tourism. The Committee also recommends that special emphasis on domestic marketing of North-Eastern region as a premier tourism
 products must be laid.   The Committee feels that despite ‘Incredible India campaign’ still there is dearth of information for middle
 class domestic tourists from rural India.  Therefore, information brochures containing all details about stay, taxi/bus fares, details of
 places to see etc. should be widely circulated all over the country through state tourism Departments.  The Committee further
 recommends that provision for budget hotels, specially, targeting domestic tourists from middle income group should be made at all
 important destinations.  It appears to the Committee that specific focused efforts for establishing contact with the expanding middle
 class budget tourists is conspicuous by its absence in the initial information circulated by the Ministry. The initial information brochure
 should be made available to foreign tourists as well giving initial details which would target budget tourists segments.
(Para 46)
OVERSEAS PROMOTION AND MARKETING
 
            The Committee appreciates the concerted efforts taken by the Ministry in positioning and marketing of Indiatourism products
 overseas under the brand "Incredible India".  The Committee feels that upgrading and enhancing of Incredible India brand should
 continue and Ministry should provide increased funds for strategic and marketing promotion across the globe to enhance India's share
 of international arrivals from 0.38% to at least 0.62% by 2007. However, the Committee is constrained to note that eastern and south-
eastern countries viz. Japan, North/South Korea, Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand and China have been ignored and all efforts of the
 Ministry aim at marketing products only in western countries.  This fact is more evident that there is no Indiatourism office in Thailand,
 Korea and China.  The Committee recommends that Government should also concentrate on the eastern countries to attract tourists
 from these countries to India, including Buddhist pilgrims.  The Committee also recommends to look into the possibility of setting-up
 overseas offices in eastern countries especially in Thailand, Korea and China.
(Para 52)
 
COORDINATION BETWEEN MINISTRY OF TOURISM AND MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION
           
The Committee notes that Ministry of Civil Aviation and Ministry of Tourism are working in close coordination with each other
 for the growth of travel & tourism sector in the country. However, the Committee strongly feels that a restrictive air transport policy
 has a very deleterious impact on the volume of tourist traffic and recommends for a more liberal aviation regimes and a open sky policy
 for the development of tourism.
(Para 57)
 
COORDINATION BETWEEN MINISTRY OF TOURISM AND MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS
           
The Committee notes that the task force on infrastructure for tourism has taken up the matter for revival of project for
 establishment of 100 hotels at railway stations by the Indian Railways. The Committee feels that the cause of domestic tourism could
 better be addressed by promoting amenities and facilities for budget tourists.  In this connection, the Committee reiterates its earlier
 recommendation contained in 66
th Report on Demands for Grants of Department of Tourism (2003-04), which is reproduced below:-
"The Committee recommends that the Department of Tourism should take up with Ministry of Railways for
 equipping the Railway service to meet the growing travel requirements of domestic and foreign tourists. Besides, better
 hotel accommodation should be provided nearer to railway stations, airports etc. such as to cater to the requirements of
 the NRI’s as the existing ones are not up to the standard of NRI’s/foreign tourists.  The Ministry of Railway may be
 persuaded to introduce ‘Special Tourist Trains’ on the pattern of Rajdhani/Shatabdi trains with fewer compartments to
 run on experimental basis on the Buddhist Circuit, which is proposed to be developed soon. For this purpose possibility
 of getting foreign assistance and Private Sector participation should also be fully explored.  Simultaneously, the
 Department of Tourism must be proactive in their approach for providing the sanitation and public convenience
 facilities at the important tourist destinations.  This may be done with the involvement of State Government/Local
 bodies/Municipal Corporation."
 
            The Committee also recommends that the project "Village on wheels" as announced in the Railway Budget 2004-05 by the
 Ministry of Railways should be linked with rural tourism and the Ministry of Tourism should prepare a comprehensive tour package for
 the budget tourists to experience the exotic rural India.

            The Committee is surprised to note that a large number of tourism projects sanctioned to State Governments/Union Territories
 by the Ministry of Tourism during the 9
th Plan period either remains incomplete or were dropped.  The Committee is of the view that
 Ministry of Tourism failed to activate the State Government machinery which resulted in huge backlog of projects.  The participation of
 the States and their support is essential for tourism to flourish and spread its benefits among the host population with numerous
 benefits.  The Committee recommends the Ministry to enlist the support of the State Governments in the matter and engage the private
 sector for completion of these projects so that delay and cost overrun in execution of tourism projects can be avoided.  The Committee
 also recommends that some institutional arrangements for monitoring progress of the projects should be developed between the
 Ministry of Tourism and State Governments/UT Administrations to evolve a shared approach of action.
 (Para 68)
COORDINATION BETWEEN MINISTRY OF TOURISM AND MINISTRY OF CULTURE
           
The Committee feels that one of the key aspects of Indian tourism is the cultural tourism around the magnificent monuments
 and heritage centres located in different parts of the country.  Both foreign and domestic tourists derive immense pleasure by visiting
 these monuments which stand as glorious embodiment of our culture and heritage.  The Committee therefore, recommends that the
 Ministry of Tourism and the Ministry of Culture should make coordinated efforts for the development of tourism sector in the country.  
 
            The Committee in the foregoing paragraphs have already emphasized the need of the co-ordination among different Ministries of
 Government of India, State Governments/Private Sectors and other agencies.  However, the Committee recommends that Ministry of
 Tourism should have an institutionalized mechanism in the form of 'National Tourism Promotion Board' to co-ordinate with all
 concerned agencies.  This Board should have permanent members and there should be an executive secretariat to assist in its efforts.
(Paras 70 & 71)
 
TOURISM DEVELOPMENT IN NORTH EASTERN REGION
 
            The Committee appreciates the efforts taken by the Ministry for the development of tourism in North Eastern region.  However,
 the Committee recommends that the Ministry of Tourism should prioritise the projects, which will help in strengthening of
 infrastructure and product development in North-Eastern region, besides harnessing the national development priorities.  Since, there is
 a separate department for North-Eastern development, the Committee feels that proper coordination between the Ministry of Tourism,
 the Department of North-Eastern Region and North-East Development Council be established to help boost the tourism industry.  The
 Committee is also apprised of the fact that ground realities and law and order situation prevailing in all these North-Eastern States are
 different from each other.  Therefore, the Committee recommends that special state-wise survey should be conducted for individual
 states and tour packages should be developed accordingly.  
(Para 80)
 
UNIFORMITY AND RATIONALISATION OF TAXES ON HOSPITALITY SECTOR
           
The Committee notes that major impediments to the growth of tourism in India are multiplicity of taxes and lack of conducive
 environment for private sector investment.  The Committee feels that the high and multiplied tax structure reduces the competitiveness
 of the Indian Tourism Products.  The Committee therefore, recommends that the Ministry of Tourism after interaction with all
 appropriate agencies should draw a package/road map and follow up the matter with the Ministry of Finance, so as to evolve uniform
 tax structure for the growth of travel & tourism sector.
(Para 84)
DEVELOPMENT OF INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY FOR PROVIDING TOURISM INFORMATION
           
The Committee notes that the Ministry of Tourism has taken a major initiatives in the field of Information Technology with a
 view to benefit tourists.  The Committee feels that internet has a great impact on the marketing of Travel and Tourism and helps greatly
 in promoting tourism destinations and products which are located even in remote areas. The Committee further notes that the present
 official website on tourism has a lot of information but these are essentially static data.  Moreover, the Committee is also not clear how
 this information is getting disseminated to the potential tourists and tourism market.  Therefore, the Committee recommends that the
 website must provide for interactive space and a call center to make information 24x7x365 complaint from anywhere in the world.

 Institutes of the Hotel Management and Food Craft Institutes, which cater to the growing demand in the service sector. The Committee
 observes that the availability of trained manpower is essential to achieve excellence in the tourism sector.  The Committee recommends
 that to meet the growing demand of trained manpower in the field of Human Resource Development more Institutes be opened up in
 private sector and Ministry should set up a Deemed Central University to monitor and co-ordinate Institutions opening in the tourism
 sector.
(Para 103)
CRUISE TOURISM
 
            The Committee notes with satisfaction that the Ministry of Tourism is working with Ministry of Shipping and concerned Port
 Trusts for the development, promotion and marketing of Cruise Tourism in India.  The Committee feels that the sea travel is becoming
 increasingly popular and there is an enormous potential for its growth and expansion in India.  The Committee recommends that the
 Ministry should further explore the possibility for the development of Cruise Tourism at other beaches located in the eastern-coast in
 India.
(Para 107)
WILD LIFE TOURISM
 
The Committee notes with concern that India's great wildlife variety has not yet been developed as a tourist attraction.  The
 wildlife sanctuaries and national parks, which are the integral part of the Indian tourism product, has not been opened for facilitation of
 tourists.  However, the Committee appreciates the move of the Ministry for giving due prominence in the publicity and marketing
 campaigns to the lesser know States and the campaign focusing on India's competitive strength on the sphere of "Wellness and
 Spirituality" has been launched.  The Committee recommends that the Ministry of Tourism should co-ordinate the matter with the
 Ministry of Environment & Forests for better facilitation of tourists in the National Parks and wildlife sanctuaries. 
(Para 112)
CHARDHAM YATRA CIRCUIT
 
            The Committee appreciates the efforts taken by the Ministry of Tourism for developing Uttranchal as a most popular pilgrimage
 destination with better and upgraded facilities for tourists in Himalayan region.  The Committee recommends that the works sanctioned
 for development of Chardham Yatra Circuit should be completed in a time bound manner and the progress of work should be
 monitored for integrated development.  The Committee also desires that the Ministry of Tourism in co-ordination with the Ministry of
 Civil Aviation should start the helicopter services for Badrinath, Kedarnath and Hemkund Sahib so that the pilgrimage tourists could
 avail this facility for their travel with in short span of time.

                                                                                          R E P O R T
            The Ministry of Culture is the apex authority to preserve and protect India’s rich cultural heritage.  The Ministry of Culture
 undertakes activities that follow from the subjects allocated under the Government of India’s Allocation of Business Rules 1961, which
 include:-
                           i.         Maintenance and conservation of the country’s heritage ancient monuments and historic sites;
                         ii.         Promotion of literary, visual and performing arts;
                        iii.         Administration of libraries, museums and institutions of anthropology;
                       iv.         Maintenance, preservation and conservation of archival records and archival libraries;
                         v.         Research and development in the conservation of cultural property;
                       vi.         Observation of centenaries and anniversaries of important national personalities and events;
                      vii.         Promotion of institutions and organisations of Buddhist and Tibetan studies;
                    viii.         Promotion of institutional and individual initiatives in the field of art and culture; and
                       ix.         Entering into and implementation of cultural agreements with foreign countries.
 
2.         The functional spectrum of the Ministry is rather wide, ranging from generating cultural awareness at the grassroots level to
 promoting cultural exchanges at an international level.  Along with programmes for the preservation of India’s ancient heritage, the
 activities of the Ministry encourage and disseminate a variety of contemporary creative arts as well.  The aim of the Ministry is to
 develop ways and means through which the basic cultural and aesthetic sensibilities of the people remain active and dynamic.

ARCHAEOLOGICAL SURVEY OF INDIA

8.         The Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) was established in 1861.  It is a large organisation having its network throughout the
 country.  So far, ASI has declared 3648 monuments to be of national importance in the country.  The major activities of the ASI are
 maintenance, conservation and preservation of centrally protected monuments/sites and remains.  It also keeps developing epigraphical
 research, setting up and reorganisation of site museums and training in archaeology.  The Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) has 21
 circles and 2 mini circles at present, whose jurisdiction are by and large co-terminus with the States.  With the creation of 3 new states
 viz. Uttaranchal, Jharkhand and Chattisgarh, three new circles are being opened with effect from 1
st April 2003.  The Ministry has also
 submitted that the Archaeological Survey of India is bringing more monuments under central protection.
 
9.         The Budgetary allocation to Archaeological Survey of India for the financial year 2004-05 is as under:-

10.        The Committee was informed that Archaeological Survey of India has been allocated Rs.70 crore for the year 2004-05 at B.E.
 stage which, is Rs.22.5 crore more than the previous year allocation i.e. 2003-04 made at R.E. stage. 
 
11.        The Ministry has informed about the policy regarding archaeological exploration and excavation.  It says that the provisions
 made in the Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains Act, 1958, govern excavations in India.  The Director General
 of the Archaeological Survey of India  grants licenses to various excavation agencies, both government and autonomous, for conducting
 excavations on the recommendations of the Standing Committee of the Central Advisory Board of Archaeology (CABA).
            Criteria for selection of a site for excavation are:-
(i)
            bridging of missing gaps(s) in the cultural sequence of Indian archaeology;
 
(ii)
          throwing more light on lesser known culture; and
 
(iii)
         Salvage archaeology in the event of a site being submerged by a dam or being destroyed or damaged due to
 absolutely necessary development works, natural calamities.
 
12.        The archaeological Survey of India conducts excavations through six excavation branches located at Nagpur, Delhi, Patna,
 Bhubaneswar, Vadodara and Mysore besides the Institute of Archaeology, Prehistory Branch and 21 Circles.  An amount of Rs.7.5 crore
 has been allocated in B.E. 2004-05 under the head Archaeological Exploration and Excavations as against Rs.4.5crore allocated in B.E.
 for 2003-04.  The Ministry has informed that the increased funds of Rs.3 crore will be utilised for:-
                        i.         Carrying out multidisciplinary studies under the Sarasvati Heritage Project in respect of sites already undertaken for
 excavation;
 
                      ii.         Technical upgradation of Excavation Branches. Underwater Archaeology Wing, Building Survey Project, Epigraphy
 Branches, Prehistory Branch, Temple Survey Projects;
 
                     iii.         Carrying out simultaneous conservation of excavated remains:
                    iv.         Procuring satellite imageries; and
                      v.         Radio carbon dating various samples recovered from the excavation by Accelerator Mass Spectromepry Method now
 available at Institute of Physics, Bhubaneswar.
 
13.        The increased budgetary allocation will also be utilised for excavations and simultaneous conservation of the major excavated
 sites like (a) Dholavira (Gujarat), (b) Hatab (Gujarat), (c) Govishan, (d) Kashipur (Uttaranchal), (e) Sravasti (UP) and (f) Udaigiri
 (Orissa).
 
14.        The Underwater Archaeology Wing which has already been constituted in a nucleus form will also be expanded and suitably
 equipped/augmented.  Expeditions in collaboration with the Indian Navy have been taken up at Bangaram Island, Lakshadweep. The
 Ministry has informed that they have availed the expertise from various institutions like Indian Institutes of Technology; Central
 Building Research Institute, Roorkee; Geological Survey of India; Water and Power Consultancy  Services etc. from time to time and
 the help of Indian Navy has also been invited as and when required.
 
15.      The Committee is of the view that excavation is a highly sensitive matter and given a multi-religious, multi-ethnic context, the
 Archaeological Survey of India is playing a crucial role in strengthening our cultural harmony.  Therefore, the Committee feels that
 proper scientific consideration should be given in selection of excavation sites and no other extraneous factors should be given
 importance.  The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Archaeological Survey of India should also take into account other
 important researches being carried out by the universities and scholars of national eminence.  Before excavation the Archaeological
 Survey of India  should ensure that the site on which the work has to be started is well protected and during excavations the antiquities
 and other materials found remain secured.  The Committee recommends that the Ministry should play proactive role in preserving the

CONFIDENTIAL

 excavation findings against natural forces, thefts and other related crimes as well as communal elements who try to incite public,
 thereby creating controversies around excavations sites.  Hence, the Committee emphasises that it is better to take preventive measures
 to check such incidents rather than taking corrective measures later on.
 
16.      The Committee notes that the underwater archaeology is in a nascent stage.  However, the Ministry should also actively involve
 itself in the under water excavations going on at Dwarka by Indian Navy as they might not have necessary scientific expertise for
 proper archaeological interpretation.
 
VACANT POSTS IN ARCHAEOLOGICAL SURVEY OF INDIA
 
17.        The Ministry has informed that at present 322 posts in various categories are lying vacant in the Archaeological Survey of India
 out of the sanctioned posts of 8376.  The Ministry has further added that for some of the posts interviews and selection to Group ‘A’
 posts are under active consideration of U.P.S.C.  The Ministry has informed that in various categories posts are lying vacant e.g. Sr.
 Archaeologist-10, Dy. Sr. Archaeologist-30, Asstt. Archaeologist-56, Asstt. Archaeological Chemist-56, Dy. S.A. Engineer-11,
 Conservation Asstt. Gr-I-14, Conservation Asstt. Gr-II-12, UDC & LDC-28 and also some in other categories. 
 
18.        The Committee is unable to understand as to why such a large number of posts have been kept vacant.  The Committee is of the
 view that keeping vacant posts in crucial cadres such as, Sr. Archaeologist, Dy. Sr. Archaeologist, Asstt. Archaeologist, Asstt.
 Archaeological Chemist, Dy. S.A. Engineer, Conservation Asstt. Gr-I, Conservation Asstt. Gr-II will certainly affect the functioning of
 the Archaeological Survey of India.  Therefore, the Committee strongly recommends that the Ministry should expedite the process of
 filling the vacant posts within a definite time frame so that the execution of Conservation, Preservation and Development work of
 monuments do not suffer due to lack of manpower.   The Committee should be apprised of the progress in the matter.
 
ORIGINAL WORKS AND CONSERVATION OF MONUMENTS UNDERTAKEN BY A.S.I.
 
19.        With the commencement of the 10
th plan period, perspective plans have been prepared by all the 21 circles & two mini-circles,
 science and horticulture branch of the ASI covering over 500 monuments.  The conservation problems of the monuments under the
 protection of Archaeological Survey of India are enormous and multifarious.  Conservation work needs expertise as well as timely
 funding. The necessary funding for conservation programmes are met out of various plans and projects like, Perspective Planning,
 National Culture Fund (NCF) and Loan funding by the Japan Bank of International Co-operation (JBIC).
 
20.        The Ministry has informed that during the 10 th Five Year Plan Period over 800 schemes in various monuments and the work on
 678 schemes has already been started.  Development of cultural and eco-tourism is emphasised upon by integrating it with monuments.  
 For this purpose, cultural hubs encompassing facilities for tourists viz. Interpretation Centres, public conveniences and modern ticket
 counters would be created keeping the prominent monuments as a focal developmental point and incorporating all minor monuments
 and sites in the near vicinity.  Certain cultural hubs thus identified are:-
                           i.         Red Fort and Humayun’s Tomb in Delhi.
                         ii.         Jaisalmer and Kumbhalgarh Fort in Rajasthan
                        iii.         Sun Temple, Modhera in Gujarat.
                       iv.         Khajuraho temples, Sanchi, Bhimbetaka rock-shelters in Madhya Pradesh.
                         v.         Taj Mahal and Fatehpur Sikri in Uttar Pradesh.
                       vi.         Udaigiri and Khandagiri caves in Orissa.
                      vii.         Ajanta and Ellora Caves in Maharashtra.
                    viii.         Hampi and Pattadakal temples in Karnataka.
                       ix.         Churches and Convents, in Goa.
                         x.         Mahabalipuram, Kanchipuram and Tanjavur temples in Tamil Nadu.
 
21.        Besides, 60 Jaina monuments, under protection of Archaeological Survey of India have been identified for the conservation and
 development of monuments under Jaina Deposit funds to the tune of Rs.1286 lakh for the celebration of 2600 th years of Tirthankara
 Mahaviras Janam Kalyanak.  The agreement for the Phase-II of the Ajanta-Ellora Conservation and Tourism Development Project with
 a loan outlay of 7331 Million Yen (Rs.300 crore) is finalised, the ASI's component being 901 Million Yen (Rs.36.77 crore).  Besides
 Ajanta and Ellora Caves, other monuments such as Daultabad Fort, Pitalkhora Caves, Patnadevi temple, Aurangabad Caves, Bibi-ka
 Maqbara, Lonar temples etc. are included in the Phase-II of the project.
 
22.      The Committee appreciates various ongoing projects for conservation and development of monuments undertaken by the
 Archaeological Survey of India as a result of which a large number of tourists are visiting these monuments. The Committee agrees to
 the view that conservation problems of the monuments are enormous and multifarious. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the
 restoration and renovation work of any monuments should be done as per the prescribed scientific norms and the Archaeological

CONFIDENTIAL
file:///D/responive/Committee%20on%20Transport,%20Tourism%20and%20Culture/80threport.htm[22-10-2018 12:01:01]
 Survey of India  should try to maintain the originality of the monuments/sites of national importance while renovating these
 monuments.  The Committee also notes the guidelines issued by the Hon’ble Supreme Court related to the renovation work carried out
 in the Red Fort, wherein, the Hon’ble Court had directed the Archaeological Survey of India  to consider the opinion of various experts
 in the field.  On the basis of the directions of the Court a Committee of Experts was also constituted by the Archaeological Survey of
 India.  In view of this direction of the Hon’ble Court, the Committee recommends that the ASI on its own should try to consult experts
 in the fields of history and archaeology even without directions from the Court.  The Committee further recommends that the ASI
 should also evolve institutionalised mechanism for eliciting opinion of independent experts in the field of archaeology. 
 
PUBLICATIONS OF ARCHAEOLOGICAL SURVEY OF INDIA
23.        The Archaeological Survey of India ’s publications are being brought out under three categories i.e. Academic, Informative and
 Awareness. Under the Academic category, the series entitled Indian Archaeology- A review, which contains the reports on the various
 archaeological activities of a particular year not only of the Survey, but of all the institutions and departments concerned with
 archaeology as a specialized discipline, in the country has been taken up for publication.  The issues for the year 1998-99, 1999-2000
 and 2000-01 are in press.  The ASI has also taken up (1) Excavation Reports, (2) Epigraphical publications and reprints of out-of-stock. 
 Annual Reports and Inventory of Delhi Monuments for publication and these are at various stages of printing.  Under the informative

NATIONAL ARCHIVES OF INDIA
56.        National Archives was set up an Imperial Records Department in 1891 in Calcutta and shifted to Delhi in 1937 and renamed as
 National Archives of India after independence in 1947.  This archive is the custodian of non-current records of enduring value of
 Central Government Ministries/ Department/Offices and their predecessor bodies.  The main functions of National Archives of India
 include accession of public records for permanent preservation, care and conservation of records in its custody for posterity; preparation
 of reference media, dissemination of information; acquisition of microfilm copies of records of Indian interests from abroad; regulation
 of access to records for research and other purposes.  National Archives of India is the nodal agency for records management activities
 of the Central Government Ministries/Departments/Offices as also of PSUs.  Statutory Bodies, Corporations, Committees and
 commissions set up by the Union Government and ultimate transfer of records of enduring value to National Archives of India for
 permanent preservation and use by the posterity.  There are various ongoing schemes, viz. expansion of Records Management
 Programme, National Register of Private Records, Repair and Reprography, Administration and Library, the School of Archival Studies,
 setting up of record centre in the Eastern Zone etc.             Under the scheme of Financial Assistance for Preservation of
 Manuscripts/Rare Books, the archives provides financial assistance to voluntary organisations, educational institutions, libraries,
 museums and universities etc.  The National Archives of India has also set a target under various schemes for expansion and
 modernisation programmes.  An outlay of Rs.3 crore has been approved by the Planning Commission for the year 2004-05 against the
 proposed outlay of Rs.7.80 crore.
 
57.        The Committee appreciates the role of National Archives of India in the field of acquiring and conserving the records for
 posterity.  However, the Committee is constrained to note that for the year 2004-05 an amount of Rs.3.00 crore has been approved
 against the requirement of Rs.7.80 crore.  The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Ministry should allocate more funds to the
 National Archives of India to carry out its various schemes and projects in the current year and all ongoing schemes should be
 completed in a time bound manner.

OBSERVATION/CONCLUSIONS/RECOMMENDATIONS
AT A GLANCE
 
TENTH PLAN OUTLAY AND ANALYSIS OF THE ANNUAL PLAN 2004-05
 
The Committee notes that the plan allocation of the Ministry of Culture has been increased substantially to Rs.400.00 crore.  The
 Committee hopes that the Ministry will ensure that the enhanced allocation will be utilised optimally with due emphasis on the new
 projects undertaken during the year viz., National Mission on Monuments, Intangible Heritage and Antiquities.
 
ARCHAEOLOGICAL SURVEY OF INDIA
 
The Committee is of the view that excavation is a highly sensitive matter and given a multi-religious, multi-ethnic context, the
 Archaeological Survey of India is playing a crucial role in strengthening our cultural harmony.  Therefore, the Committee feels that
 proper scientific consideration should be given in selection of excavation sites and no other extraneous factors should be given
 importance.  The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Archaeological Survey of India should also take into account other
 important researches being carried out by the universities and scholars of national eminence.  Before excavation the Archaeological
 Survey of India  should ensure that the site on which the work has to be started is well protected and during excavations the antiquities
 and other materials found remain secured.  The Committee recommends that the Ministry should play proactive role in preserving the
 excavation findings against natural forces, thefts and other related crimes as well as communal elements who try to incite public,
 thereby creating controversies around excavations sites.  Hence, the Committee emphasises that it is better to take preventive measures
 to check such incidents rather than taking corrective measures later on.
The Committee notes that the underwater archaeology is in a nascent stage.  However, the Ministry should also actively involve
 itself in the under water excavations going on at Dwarka by Indian Navy as they might not have necessary scientific expertise for
 proper archaeological interpretation.
(Paras 15 and 16)
 
 
VACANT POSTS IN ARCHAEOLOGICAL SURVEY OF INDIA
 
The Committee is unable to understand as to why such a large number of posts have been kept vacant.  The Committee is of the view
 that keeping vacant posts in crucial cadres such as, Sr. Archaeologist, Dy. Sr. Archaeologist, Asstt. Archaeologist, Asstt. Archaeological
 Chemist, Dy. S.A. Engineer, Conservation Asstt. Gr-I, Conservation Asstt. Gr-II will certainly affect the functioning of the
 Archaeological Survey of India.  Therefore, the Committee strongly recommends that the Ministry should expedite the process of filling
 the vacant posts within a definite time frame so that the execution of Conservation, Preservation and Development work of monuments
 do not suffer due to lack of manpower.   The Committee should be apprised of the progress in the matter.
(Para 18)
 
ORIGINAL WORKS AND CONSERVATION OF MONUMENTS UNDERTAKEN BY A.S.I.
 
The Committee appreciates various ongoing projects for conservation and development of monuments undertaken by the

The Committee expresses its displeasure over the fact that various reports on the archaeological activities are pending for almost
 last six years.  The Committee is of the view that in absence of timely publication of these reports, achievements of Archaeological

The Committee expresses its concern towards the prevailing scenario of museum security all over the country especially, the

 personnel to operate on these security gadgets.  The Committee further directs the Ministry to provide museums with adequate funds to
 strengthen their security as it has been observed that except for national museum, no specific allocation has been made for the security

 Ahmedabad and would like to apprise itself about the reasons for delay in these projects.  The Committee also recommends that due
 priority should be given to Science City projects and the Ministry should actively co-ordinate with the Members of Parliament of
 respective states so as to ensure coordination and cooperation of local bodies.  The Committee directs the Ministry to generate interest
 among the private entrepreneurs since, they will be bearing major cost of these projects as per the norms prescribed by the
 Government.

 The Committee recommends that the Ministry as central monitoring agency should help implementing these missions and expedite their
 progress.
(Para 70)
 
CULTURAL EXCHANGE PROGRAMMES
 
The Committee notes that during the year 2003-04 the Cultural Exchange Programmes were signed with 21 countries, including
 China, Iran, Egypt, France, Germany, Greece, Brazil, Hungary and South Africa and out of 114, there are 82 countries with whom,
 specific biennial and triennial cultural exchange programmes have been entered into.   However, the Committee is constrained to note
 that the Ministry could not utilise the sanctioned money to strengthen cultural relations with other countries.  The Committee
 recommends the Ministry to give priority to cultural exchange programmes since, healthy cultural relations with other countries not only
 promote India’s image abroad but also function as a catalytic to boost foreign tourism.
(Para 74)
FESTIVALS OF INDIA

CONFIDENTIAL
file:///D/responive/Committee%20on%20Transport,%20Tourism%20and%20Culture/80threport.htm[22-10-2018 12:01:01]
 
The Committee notes that there are various proposals for holding Festival of India in different countries viz. Brazil, Singapore
 and Iran which are under consideration.  The Committee recommends that such festivals should be organised on regular basis for
 propagation of our culture and tradition abroad and opening venues for tourism in the country.  The Committee feels that the budgetary
 allocation made for this purpose is insufficient, since, in one such festival which was held at Bhutan, the Ministry has spent Rs.120
 lakh.  Hence, an increase of Rs.40 lakh in B.E. 2004-05 may not be sufficient and recommends that Ministry should arrange for more
 funds.  The Committee also recommends that the Ministry should take initiatives to co-ordinate with various regional co-operative
 associations such as SAARC, ASEAN, BIMSTEC which will strengthen our cultural linkages with neighbouring countries.
(Para 77)
 
NORTH EAST REGION
 
The Committee is satisfied with the progress regarding various activities taken up by the Ministry in order to give publicity to
 diverse art and culture of the North-Eastern States, including Sikkim.  For North-Eastern States Rs.3545 lakh has been allocated in B.E.
 2004-05 as against Rs.2250 lakh in R.E. 2003-04.  The Committee observes that during the year 2003-04 no major initiative/project has
 been taken by the Ministry in the States of Nagaland and Arunachal Pradesh.  Therefore, the Committee recommends that more
 activities and schemes should be implemented in these States in view of the increased allocation.  The Committee feels that the North-
Eastern Region is considered to be at disadvantageous position owing to its geographical isolation and poor  infrastructure, due to which
 cultural heritage of these states remains in darkness. The Committee recommends  that the Ministry of Culture should have proactive
 measures to project cultural realities and diversities of North-Eastern Regions to the rest of the country.
(Para 83)
 
CO-ORDINATION BETWEEN THE MINISTRIES OF TOURISM, CULTURE AND ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS
 
The Committee expresses its displeasure over the fact that the Ministry has not taken up the matter of setting up of Co-ordination
 Committee with regard to the projects for integrated development, conservation and preservations of monuments.  The Committee
 recommends that the Co-ordination Committee should be set up for this purpose at the earliest.  The Committee further recommends
 that the Ministry will co-ordinate with Ministry of Road Transport and Highways regarding linking of roads to give connectivity to all
 the monuments of national importance. The Committee, strongly feels that the Ministry of Culture should make concerted efforts for the
 holistic development of monuments/sites.
(Para 85)
 
UNESCO AND WORLD HERITAGE SITES IN INDIA
 
The Committee appreciates the initiatives taken by the Ministry for inclusion of more sites in the World Heritage List of the
 UNESCO, as a result of which for the first time the UNESCO has declared 3 monuments of India as World Heritages within one year. 
 However, the Committee further recommends that same efforts may be continued in future also so that more number of monuments can
 be enlisted as World Heritages in view of the vast and rich cultural heritage of our country.
(Para 90)

INTERNATIONAL SHIP AND PORT FACILITY SECURITY
 
25.       The International Maritime Organization (IMO) has introduced new maritime security regulations called International Code for the
 Security of Ships and of Port Facility (ISPS Code) which was adopted as an amendment to 'Safety of Life at Sea (SOLAS)' by the conference
 of Contracting Governments on 12/12/2002.  The ISPS Code embodies a number of functional requirements which include:
 
(i)         gathering and assessing information with respect to security threats and exchanging such information with appropriate Contracting
 Governments;
(ii)        requiring the maintenance of communication protocols for ships and port facilities;
(iii)       preventing unauthorized access to ships, port facilities and their restricted areas;
(iv)       preventing the introduction of unauthorized weapons, incendiary devices or explosives to ships or port facilities;
(v)        providing means for raising the alarm in reaction to security threats or security incidents;
(vi)       requiring ship and port facility security plans based upon security assessments; and
(vii)      requiring training, drills and exercises to ensure familiarity with security plans and procedures.
 
26.       The code was introduced as a fall out of 11 th September 2001 terrorist attack incident in the US, after which the need to tighten up
 security for all modes of transport, was realised.  Therefore, the 22 nd Session of the Assembly of the IMO in November, 2001 unanimously
 agreed to the development of new measures relating to the security of ships and of port facilities for adoption by a Conference of Contracting
 Governments to the SOLAS (Safety of Life at Sea) 1974.  The ISPS Code provides for the international framework through which ship and
 port facilities can cooperate to detect and deter acts which threaten security in the maritime transport sector. The Code has become mandatory
 with effect from 1st July, 2004 in respect of the contracting parties to SOLAS 1974 including India.
 
27.       Giving the details of efforts made to implement the new security regulations in India the Ministry informed the Committee that the
 ISPS Code in India covers all Major Ports, Minor Ports catering to international trade, and Ships.  Under the Code if an ISPS compliant Ship
 enters a non-compliant Port, it will have problems in its next voyage which will affect international trade and business.  India is one among
 the first few countries to complete implementation of ISPS Code, ensuring that there will be no hindrance in Indian exports and imports.
 
28.       All Indian Ships, Major Ports and Minor Ports in the country have since been completed and Port facility security plans (PFSP) have
 also been prepared by the DG(Shipping).
 
29.       During the course of oral evidence, the Secretary informed the Committee that;
"the international code for security of ships and ports facility was a fall-out of 9/11 attack in US on the World Trade center.  IMO
 introduced the ISPS Code which has come into effect from 1.7.2004.  In India too, we have covered all major and minor ports catering to
 international trade and all ships above 500 GT.  The DG(S) has been made the designated authority for this purpose and the Indian Register of
 Shipping the recognized organisation for this purpose. Accordingly, all the 12 Major Ports, 34 minor ports and 191 ships flying the Indian
 Flag have become ISPS-complaint;"
           
30.       The Committee appreciates the Ministry for complying the ISPS code for all 12 Major Ports, 34 minor ports catering to international
 trade and 191 Indian Flagged ships in the country.  The Committee notes that the new maritime security regulations will provide international
 framework for ships and ports facilities besides detecting the deterring acts, which threaten security in the maritime transport sector.  The
 implementation of ISPS code, will also do away the hindrances in Indian export and imports.  The Committee, however, recommends that a
 task force be formed in the Ministry to observe strict compliance of international safety and security code/regulations.

INDIAN SEAFARERS WORKING ON FOREIGN FLAGGED SHIPS
 
40.       Indian seafarers working on foreign flagged vessels enjoy tax free status, as they are in more advantageous position to comply with
 the requirements to become eligible to NRI status when they are employed on Indian ships.  Even when they do no comply with the
 requirements to become eligible for NRI status, they are not subject to TDS in India, because the foreign ship owners employing Indian
 seafarers are outside the jurisdiction of the Indian Tax authorities. 
41.       On a question of exempting the Indian seafarers from paying taxes so as to retain qualified and trained officers, the Ministry
 informed that as a measure of preventing the large-scale drift of qualified and experienced personnel, Sec.6 of I.T. Act was amended in
 1990 to provide for tax exemption in respect of income received by the Indian crew serving on Indian ships outside India for 182 or more
 days in a year. The provision was aimed specifically to help Indian shipping companies to retain the services of Indian crew employed on
 their ships.  However, this intent could not be achieved because of an interpretation of the relevant provision namely, Explanation (a) to
 Sub-Section (1)(c) of Sec.6 by CBDT Circular No.586 of 28-11-1990 that the period of the seafarers’ service when the ships are in Indian
 territorial waters is to be treated as period of service in India, in a year.  A communication dated May 7, 1996 received from CBDT clarified
 this point.  As Indian ships generally operate in international waters and also call frequently at Indian ports, a large number of the crew
 employed on Indian ships though trading outside India cannot comply with this eligibility criteria to have NRI status, resulting in denial of
 tax exemption benefits to most of Indian seafarers working on Indian ships.
 
42.       An expert committee under the chairmanship of Dr. Rakesh Mohan, the then Adviser to the Finance Minister was constituted in
 August, 2001. The committee considered this issue after taking into consideration various alternatives and recommended “In order to make
 employment on Indian ships attractive vis-à-vis foreign ships, it is essential that Indian nationals serving on board Indian flag ships be
 treated equally as those Indians employed on foreign ships. The Committee also recommended for insertion of appropriate provision in
 Sec.10 of the Income Tax Act and the alternative, the Board in exercise of its power under Sec.119 of the Act may issue a Circular that
 would put an end to the discriminatory consequences of the CBDT Circular of 28-11-1990, though such discrimination was unintended”.
 
43.       In line with the recommendation of the committee, following provision/clarification (as a sub-section inserted in Section 10 of the
 I.T. Act) is suggested for consideration of CBDT:
“In case of an Indian citizen who is a member of the crew of an Indian ship as defined in clause (18) of section 3 of the Merchant
 Shipping Act, 1958, any income chargeable under the head “Salaries” received by or due to any such individual being a non-resident as
 remuneration for services rendered in connection with his employment on such ship where his total stay in India does not exceed in the
 aggregate a period of 182 days in the previous year and where actual period/s of stay outside India of such individual while serving on such
 ship/s is determined as under :-          
“His stay in India may be determined from the embarkation date stamped by the Immigration authority on his passport or by the
 Master of vessel on the Articles of Agreement (Foreign Going), whichever is earlier, to the disembarkation date stamped on the passport or
 on CDC while signing-off from the ship, whichever is later.”
 
44.       The Ministry has been taking up the recommendation of the committee with the Ministry of Finance at various levels since 2002 and
 has suggested necessary amendments in the Income Tax Act so as to provide necessary relief to the deprived Indian seafarers.  Response
 from Ministry of Finance is still awaited in the matter.
 
45.       During the course of evidence, the Secretary deposed before the Committee that;
"the request of seamen to get exemption from Income tax deserves consideration.  This will encourage seafaring profession in India,

 to go on board the foreign-flag vessels.  Today he gets the income exemption while working on the Indian ships- only, and only if he

INLAND WATER TRANSPORT
 85.      Inland waterways comprises of rivers, creeks, canals, backwaters and lakes etc. which extend to about 14,500 kms length in the
 country out of which about 5,700 kms are navigable by mechanised vessels.  However, the potential of this important mode of transport has
 not been exploited so far to its desired level. Inland Water Transport (IWT) schemes mainly relate to development of waterways and
 augmentation of the traffic carrying capacity through expansion and modernization of I.W.T. vessels.  Whereas the Inland Waterways
 Authority of India (IWAI) is responsible for the development of National Waterways, responsibility for the development of State
 Waterways rests with the State Governments.  The Central Government have declared three Waterways, viz., Allahabad – Haldia Stretch
 (1620 kms.) Sadiya and Dhubri Stretch (891 kms.)  and  West Coast Canal from  Kollam to Kottapuram stretch along with  Udyogamandal
 and Champakara canals  (total 205 km) as National Waterways. Amongst the major initiatives, during the 10th Plan, it has been planned to
 construct Permanent Terminals at Gaighat, Patna, in N.W.- I and at Pandu, Assam, in NW-II. During the Financial Year 2004-05, a sum of
 Rs.145.57 crores (including Rs.47.5 crore from NE Pool) has been earmarked towards Plan Support to IWAI.
                       
86.       IWAI undertakes various schemes related to development of IWT infrastructure on these three National Waterways namely, Fairway
 Development, Terminals and Navigational Aids.  The Committee desired to know about the status of the proposal for declaration of four
 Waterways as National Waterways on the basis of techno-economic feasibility studies conducted by IWAI. The Ministry informed that the
 National Transport Policy Committee (NTPC) had identified 10 waterways.  Out of these three waterways namely the Ganga-Bhagirathi-
Hooghly, the Brahmaputra and the West Coast Canal have already been declared as National Waterways.  The Ministry further informed
 that a view was earlier taken by the Ministry that no new waterways  would be declare as National Waterways until the existing National
 Waterways are made fully operational. The policy has since been reviewed by the Ministry. Accordingly, the following three proposals for
 declaration as National Waterways are being pursued:
 
(i)         Godavari-Krishna and the integrated canal system including Buckingham            Canal in Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu –
1074 kms.
(ii)        The Barak River in the Silichar Valley in North-East – 140 km.
(iii)       The East Coast Canal alongwith Brahmani river and Mahanadi Delta in Orissa – 623 kms.

 North-East, the same will be considered in order of its priority.

(v)  Encouraging private sector participation in Inland Water Transport.
(vi) Making existing National Waterways fully functional by providing necessary infrastructure in a time bound       manner.
 
92.       Regarding comparative cost effective evaluation for transportation of cargo through this alternate mode of transport, the Ministry
 informed that no authentic study has been done so far in general terms, even though, NCAER has done a study on NW-1 in 1991,
 concluding that per tonne-km cost of IWT is less than road but slightly more than the rail mode.  IWAI is being asked to commission a
 study to make comparative cost effective evaluation of IWT mode in the context of door to door freight transportation in certain selected
 sectors.

                        " At the end of 9
th Five Year Plan the cargo handled in the Inland Water Transport Sector was 1.5 billion tonne-kilometers. 
 During 2003-04 this figure touched 1.7 billion tonne-kilometers.  Tonne- Kilometre is a unit used in Inland Water Transport sector across
 the globe and is a measure of a tonne of cargo being transported one kilometer.

 have been taken in hand.  The targets fixed for providing 24-hour navigation in National Waterways are as under:-

2.      National Waterway No.2:- 24-hour navigation facilities are already provided from Bangladesh Border to Chandradinga
 (84 kms).   The facilities are being further extended upto Neamati by March, 2005 and upto dibrugarh by December, 2005.

Edapallikotta stretch by December, 2004.  Remaining portion of NW 3 will be brought under night navigation facilities by

During the year 2003-04, an amount of Rs.86.82 crore has been spent on Inland Water Transport development.  In 2002-03 this
 figure was only Rs.55.36 crore.
 
            Inland Water Transport is a potential area and should receive national priority.  The question is often asked why we are not
 witnessing large scale movement of cargo through Inland Water Transport.  My answer to this, would be that in our country the
 investment needed for reviving the Inland Water Transport mode o transport has been inadequate.  World-wide, it has been experienced
 that with the growth of efficient road and rail network, traditional mode of Inland Water Transport declines.  But it may be revived if
 Government comes out with necessary policy support and adequate investments.  In our country, this support has been sub-optimal.  For
 the declared 3 NWs, we have so far spent Rs.292.74 crore only in the last 18 years.  If we have to achieve the stated objective of making
 these 3 NWs fully operational even by the end of 10 th Five Year Plan, there is a need of additional Rs.293 crore of plan funds over and
 above the available provision of Rs.301 crore in the remaining period of 10th Five Year Plan."

94.       The Committee expresses its concern over the slow pace of development of Inland Water Transport sector in the country.  The
 Committee feels that the potential of this important mode of transport has not yet been exploited to its desired level.  The Committee is
 surprised to note that inspite of the efforts of the Government only Rs.292.74 crore was spent during the last 18 years for development of
 the existing three National Waterways.  The Committee disapproves the lackadaisical approach of the Ministry towards the development of
 this important mode of transport. The Committee however, notes that a policy frame-work for the Inland Water Transport system has been
 approved by the Government to mobilize the required resources by attracting private investments and forming joint ventures for developing
 waterways infrastructure and cargo handling facilities. The Committee is however, constrained to express its doubts over the participation
 of private sector unless the Government has focused approach for providing basic infrastructural facilities for Inland Water Transport.
 
95.       The Committee is constrained to note that cargo transportation by Inland Water Transport mode has not shown significant
 improvement on these three National Waterways.  The Committee also expresses its displeasure over the fact that no comparative cost-
output evaluation for transportation of cargo through this alternate mode of transport has been carried out by the Ministry. The Committee is
 of the view that such evaluation would further establish the support of Inland Water Transport over other mode of transports. Therefore, the
 Committee recommends that a detailed study should be carried out by the Ministry in this regard. The Committee also recommends the
 Ministry to look into the possibility of formation of the taskforce to oversee the progress of the projects so that these could be completed in
 a time bound manner for development of Inland Water Transport in country.   The Committee feels that there is a need to strengthen R&D
 facilities particularly in the design of vessels, night navigation facilities, identification of economically viable routes and issues of mutual
 benefits with neighbouring countries like Bangladesh.  In this context, the Committee also reiterates its earlier recommendation contained in
 its 70th Report of Demands for Grants (2003-04) of the Ministry of Shipping, which is reproduce below;
"The Committee also does not approve the strategy of the Ministry to make investment for development and regulation of Inland
 Waterways without fixing the physical targets to be achieved vis-à-vis financial parameter. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the
 Ministry while coming up with target of investment must have a realistic physical target for cargo transportation, year-wise for the entire
 10th Plan period and beyond."
 
96.       The Committee further recommends that the Ministry should approach the Ministry of Finance to enhance allocation by Rs.293 crore
 as requested by the Secretary, Ministry of Shipping for the remaining period of 10 th Plan so as to achieve the objectives of making the
 existing three National Waterways fully operational.

97.       The Central Inland Water Transport Corporation Ltd., CIWTC Ltd. is engaged in transportation of cargo through Inland Waterways
 in the country and in the routes identified in the Protocol on Inland Water Transport between India and Bangladesh.    In addition, it offers
 services in the area of construction and repair of small and medium sized IWT /Coastal vessels at its Rajabagan Dockyard.  The authorised
 share capital of the company as on 31.03.2004 is Rs. 150.00 crores with a paid-up capital of Rs.127.49 crore.  The existing fleet strength of
 the Central Inland Water Transport Corporation is about 100 vessels, out of which 52 vessels are operational and 22 vessels are under

100.     Regarding  revival plan of Central Inland Water Transport Corporation the Ministry informed that a revival package approved by the
 Cabinet on 26.6.01 for the revival of the Central Inland Water Transport Corporation is under implementation.  The revival package
 envisaged the following :-

(ii)        Strengthening the River Service Division, Closure of Deep Sea Ship Repair Division and have only a small Ship Repair Division to
 carry out minor/running repairs of CIWTC fleet and closing/down sizing the activities of the RBD of CIWTC by reorganization of these

101.     Besides, the cost of the revival package was worked out at Rs. 139.55 crore which was to be financed by budgetary support of Rs.
 76.55 crore, loan re-payable from sale proceeds of surplus land and assets of Rs. 39.67 crore and sale of surplus land and assets, of Rs.
 23.33 crore.  The Government have released Rs. 65.80 crore during the first year of revival i.e. 2001-02, Rs. 62.55 crore in the year 2002-03
 and Rs. 16.08 crore during the year 2003-04.
 
102.     Many components of the revival package (except the sale of surplus land and closure and sale of Rajabagan Dockyard) have been, by
 and large implemented.  However, physical and financial performance of the Corporation has not improved.  In view of this, Ministry is
 considering refinements in the revival package sanctioned earlier.

 involving Government assistance of Rs.139 crore.  However, the Committee also note that there is a dispute over the time-frame of
 restructuring plan, the exact time of starting of the scheme and availability of funds. Given the fact that inspite of substantial investment for
 infrastructure building in Inland Water Transport sector and the insignificant participation of private sector in utilizing infrastructure for the
 restructuring the Central Inland Water Transport Corporation to a proper health is an urgent task.  Therefore, the Committee is of the view
 that the future of IWT operations including that of CIWTC holds immense possibilities for establishing a well-defined multimodal
 transportation network in the country and recommends that Government should consider a fresh financial restructuring of the company.

OBSERVATION/CONCLUSIONS/RECOMMENDATIONS
AT A GLANCE
 
ANYLYSIS OF ANNUAL PLAN 2004-05
            The Committee expresses its dissatisfaction on the fact that there has been a heavy shortfall in the utilisation of funds as compared to
 approved outlay.  During 2003-04, out of the total outlay of Rs.2543.90 crore the Ministry could spent only Rs.1104.70 crore.  It indicates
 that while proposing its plan outlay, the Ministry of Shipping had not been realistic in its approach.  However, the Committee feels that the
 complete utilisation of approved outlay could have definitely helped in improving the schemes/projects undertaken by the Ministry of
 Shipping.  The Committee recommends that in future, the Ministry should have realistic planning, so that the approved outlay can be
 utilised fully.
(Para 9)

PORT SECTOR
            The Committee notes with dismay that during the annual plan 2003-04, an allocation of Rs.1479.55 crore was approved for the Port
 Sector but the Ports could utilise only Rs.347.87 crore resulting into a heavy shortfull of Rs.1131.68 crore in the utilisation of budgetary
 allocations.  The Committee does not approve the reasons as detailed by the Ministry of Shipping for the shortfall.  The Committee fails to
 understand as to how the physical targets will be achieved with this low utilisation pattern.  In fact, the Committee feels that this raises
 doubts about the mismatch in the projections for physical and financial targets.  The Committee is of the view that the Ministry of Shipping
 has full responsibility to ensure proper utilisation of the approved outlay.  The Committee feels that strict monitoring is crucial for timely
 completion of any project.  Therefore, the Committee recommends that the monitoring agency should play rather proactive role and do
 away with the procedural hurdles for timely completion of the projects so that the budgeted allocation is utilised optimally.  The Committee
 also recommends the Ministry to keep informed about the progress in the matter.
(Para 17)
CAPACITY AND TRAFFIC IN MAJOR PORT
         The Committee notes that the Ministry is taking capacity building major schemes for improving the capacity and productivity of all
 Major Ports.  The Committee appreciates the Ministry for adding capacity of 46.05 MTPA to Ports in the first two years of the 10 th Plan,
 making the aggregate cargo handling capacity of Port to 390 MTPA as against the total traffic of 344.53 MT.  The Committee observes that
 aggregate capacity of the Major Ports exceeds the traffic targets.  The Committee, therefore, recommends the Ministry to initiate action for
 the modernization and capacity expansion of the port network across India's maritime zone so as to enable the Ports to utilise the additional
 capacity vis-à-vis traffic smoothly.
(Para 24)
INTERNATIONAL SHIP AND PORT FACILITY SECURITY
            
The Committee appreciates the Ministry for complying the ISPS code for all 12 Major Ports, 34 minor ports catering to international
 trade and 191 Indian Flagged ships in the country.  The Committee notes that the new maritime security regulations will provide international
 framework for ships and ports facilities besides detecting the deterring acts, which threaten security in the maritime transport sector.  The
 implementation of ISPS code, will also do away the hindrances in Indian export and imports.  The Committee, however, recommends that a
 task force be formed in the Ministry to observe strict compliance of international safety and security code/regulations.
(Para 30)
SAGAR MALA
            The Committee is happy to note that Sagar Mala programme has been initiated to cover all facets of maritime transport including Ports,
 Shipping and Inland Waterways with the aim to fully realise the potential of sea-borne trade and Inland Water Transport system.  The
 Committee feels that any delay in cabinet approval of this programme will adversely affect the modernization alongwith capacity expansion
 of ports network in the country.  However, the Committee is constrained to note that there is very little activity in the Inland Water Transport
 sub-sector.  This raises the question that how investment on infrastructure building will yield commensurate economically viable rate of
 returns.  The Committee was also disturbed to note that the IWAI is yet to develop the infrastructure for capacity building both in terms of
 human resources for proper technology appraisal, R&D and design inducement packages.  Therefore, the Committee concludes that this is a
 task, which should be urgently addressed.    The Committee, therefore, recommends that an early approval to launch Sagar Mala programme
 should be given and the Ministry should initiate action for setting-up of Sagar Mala Development Authority on the pattern of National
 Highways Authority of India.
(Para 36)
INTRODUCING OF TONNAGE TAX
            
The Committee notes that the Government has since introduced the tonnage tax in lieu of the corporate tax as per its
 recommendation.  The Committee hopes that with the introduction of tonnage tax and other fiscal incentives, the Indian Shipping
 companies will be able to acquire more tonnage.  However, the Committee is constrained to note that at present, the tonnage tax scheme is
 proposed for the vessels registered under the Merchant Shipping Act, 1958 only and vessels registered under the Indian Vessels Act, 1917,
 Indian Coastal Act 1838 and Dredgers have not been included for the purpose.  The Committee, therefor, recommends that in order to
 promote Inland Water Transport in the country, the Ministry should pursue the matter with Ministry of Finance for extending the benefit of
 tonnage tax to Dredgers and vessels registered under Indian Vessels/Indian Coastal Vessels Acts. 
(Para 39)
INDIAN SEAFARES WORKING ON FOREIGN FLAGGED SHIPS
           
The Committee expresses its deep concern regarding continuing drift of personnels away from employment on Indian ship to foreign
 flagged ships.  The Committee notes that the drift is due to lack of uniform tax regime i.e. Indian officers on Indian Ships have to pay
 income tax whereas, Indian officers on foreign flagged vessels are enjoying tax free status.  The Committee feels that there is some lacunae
 in the CBDT circular dated 28.11.90.  The Committee, recommends, the Ministry to revisit the whole issue in order to make employment on
 Indian ships attractive vis-à-vis foreign ships, and if necessary, impress upon the Ministry of Finance for amendment in the Income Tax
 Act.
(Para 46)

KOLKATA DOCK LABOUR BOARD
The Committee notes with anguish that the Kolkata Dock Labour Board has not yet revised the pension and liberalisation of post
 retirement benefits in terms of wage settlement and the pensioners have not been paid their pensionary and other post retirement dues for
 long.  The Committee notes that Kolkata Dock Labour Board, a body corporate, was constituted in terms of Section 5 (A) of the Dock
 Workers (Regulation of Employment) Act, 1948 in September 1952.  However, the Committee is constrained to note that the employees of
 the Board are not being treated as a Government employees so far as payment of pension and pensionary benefits to the employees of
 Kolkata Dock Labour Board is concerned, which is a matter of right of the Government employees.  The Committee also notes with
 constrained that Kolkata Dock Labour Board has also not been provided financial assistance out of the National Revival Fund. The
 Committee notes that a proposal for release of one time grant of Rs.42.96 crore to Kolkata Dock Labour Board was sent to the Ministry of
 Finance but the Ministry of Finance has not acceded to the request for release of grants to Kolkata Dock Labour Board.  The Committee is
 of the view that it is the sole liability of the Government to pay pension to the pensioners in time and it will be sheer discrimination on the
 part of the Government to withhold pension and post retirement benefits in the name of financial crisis that prevailed in Kolkata Dock
 Labour Board.  Therefore, the Committee strongly recommends that no injustice should be meted to the pensioners of Kolkata Dock Labour
 Board in the payment of pension and pensionary benefits and the Ministry of Shipping should impress upon the Ministry of Finance for
 release of one time grant for the implementation the pensionary and other benefits to the pensioners.   In fact even Voluntary Retirement
 Scheme could be implemented to address this serious problem.  The Committee also recommends the Ministry to keep it informed about the
 progress in the matter regularly.

The Committee is not satisfied with replies of the Ministry regarding setting up of Indian Maritime University, terms and conditions
 of employees creation of Pension Fund and retention of Government accommodation etc. and convey its dismay over the delay in
 finalisation of terms and conditions of service of Indian Institute of Maritime Studies and confusion is still prevailing in this regard, this has
 certainly affect the morale of the employees.  The Committee is of the view that the creation of trust for the Indian Institute of Maritime
 Studies has resulted in ambiguity with respect to the management of funds of Indian Institute of Maritime Studies.  The Committee,
 therefore, recommends that Government must expedite their effort for formation of university for Indian Institute of Maritime Studies. In
 this connection, the Committee reiterates its earlier recommendation contained in the 70th Report
of Demands for Grants 2003-04 of the Ministry of Shipping which is reproduce below:
 
"The Committee, however, recommends that the Ministry should go for establishing the University by an Act of Parliament so as to
 provide considerable operational freedom and a qualitative boost to the Maritime training in the country.  The Committee, however, notes
 with concern that the terms and conditions of services are being changed against the interest of the employees.   The Committee
 recommends that before taking any action with regard to the terms and conditions of the service of employees of erstwhile Maritime
 Institutes, the unions of the employees be consulted and it should be ensured that the terms and conditions of service of employees who
 have been transferred on deemed deputation to IIMS remain unchanged. Also, the interests of employees particularly relating to pension,
 CGHS facilities and retention of Government accommodation should be safeguarded."

 with Ministry of Finance for providing a grant to the extent of Rs.92.78 crore to recoup the shortage in the Seamen's Provident Fund.  More
